articles.title: ANT, the IPO of the Century
articles.content:
Hey Everyone,
So Anthropic’s IPO represents a major turning point in the history of Generative AI. Anthropic was founded on January 26, 2021, just five years and nine months ago. Anthropic was basically an ideologically walkout of talent from OpenAI.
Together just these two companies have raised $428.4 Billion to date not counting proceeds from the IPO. Over the past five years (2021 to 2026), the BigAI duopoly, just these two startups have raised around 27% (more than a quarter) of all AI funding to startups. Along with the backing of BigTech, this is textbook unfair advantages.
Anthropic could possibly be not just the technology IPO of the decade or our generation, but of the century. Anthropic has thus managed to attract and retain top AI researcher and now executive talent.
Expected to go public on Thursday, November 19th in the afternoon perhaps around 1:30 pm, Anthropic has priced its IPO at $83 per share, and an IPO where retail investors themselves are likely to be far more bullish about Anthropic than they were about SpaceX.
The split of Anthropic with OpenAI stemmed from disagreements over OpenAI's direction—specifically concerns among the departing team that OpenAI was prioritizing rapid commercialization (after the Microsoft deal), a position Anthropic now finds itself in itself not even six years from its founding. Torn between a mandate of AI alignment while radically pitching recursive self-improvement as a selling point, and needing so much (almost too much) compute, it’s hard to say where Anthropic will land in the 2030s, or even in the decade ahead.
How the IPO is received could shape much of Nvidia’s fall. Anthropic is the singular frontier lab and product company to watch in 2027 and takes over being the focal point of the AI boom. I no longer consider OpenAI or Google a peer in LLMs with Anthropic. However my opinion is not yet unanimous consensus.
According to Epoch AI, Anthropic’s compute spending is increasing by 4x per year, outpacing OpenAI’s 3x. For all of Anthropic’s antics about trust & saftey, we’ve never seen BigTech spawn a child company quite like this! An IPO where Alphabet (Google) and Amazon will own a 28% equity stake in the company tied to hyperscaler (Cloud computing) incentives and TPUs, the AI chips of Google.
How do you justify a young startup with a market valuation of roughly $1.49 trillion on a fully diluted basis, one that makes the world’s best frontier AI models? With Nvidia seemingly no longer the poster child of the AI trade, can Anthropic take its place for the IPO boom period? We’ll know more in the next few weeks. It may ultimately depend on how well Anthropic transitions to a product-company for Enterprise. While Anthropic’s revenue ramp is indeed historic, margins and compute costs will be something to watch.
Anthropic should raise in the area of $94.48 billion in gross proceeds significantly boosting its cash position while entering a shaky AI correction market where both AI related semiconductor and compute related Neo Clouds have been under significant pressure over the last few weeks. It remains to be seen how Anthropic’s identity will morph as a public company - which could move as fast as its products. In theory, Anthropic is an AI research and products company based in San Francisco that builds Claude, and that family of large language models supposedly treating AI safety as a core part of its mission. Anthropic, the fastest revenue growth startup of tech history. How will they deal with that level of success and those expectations?
If this is the dominant Enterprise AI company of our generation, we should not judge it too hastily or too soon. Using its products however is part of our journey for those of us who want to keep up with Generative AI’s pace of developments. This is the main reason when obtaining guest posts from Substack’s considerable talent base, my primary focus is helping my readers use Claude. The agent skills for finance tasks are only going to get better.

articles.title: Grok Bot vs Dots: Which is the better personal agent?
articles.content:
Good Morning,
This week amid mysterious tech outrages, the backdrop of the most important person in tech unable to return to his own company - Nvidia Earnings and Anthropic’s IPO, almost feel coincidental? The same week Google announced the era of AI autonomous attacks has arrived.
I wanted to continue our theme for the month of hands on applied AI guides. Our guest writer today has a Black Friday deal on his Newsletter, kindly check it out.
The Cursor team at SpaceX’s AI unit truly are outstanding. This to me what also makes Grok Bot vs. Anthropic’s Duet vs. OpenAI Dots a fairly interesting thing to watch for in 2027. Which one do you find yourself using the most?
It can’t be a coincidence that OpenAI is getting lawsuits over its cybersecurity breaking Astra-in-training and that this week first Microsoft, then the FAA, then the banks, and the NSA, and Apple iCloud all had issues, right? While Alibaba Qwen and OpenAI released new models, nobody seemed to notice. Google at the frontier, not quite. Jensanity indeed!
Anthropic is slated to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol “ANT” and start trading on Nov. 19. How could a five year old go company in under half the usual time with this much revenue growth? Anthropic will turn just six on January 26th, 2027. Every model and product it launches, we have to pay attention to.
Claude seems to be about to spawn its own software-AI universe:
Claude Meetings
Claude Whiteboards, Sheets, etc…
Whatever Claude Duet can become is going to be pretty interesting.
We were just getting used to Claude Fable 5.2 after all.
Nvidia still has more revenue in a single Quarter, nearly $116 Billion than Anthropic and OpenAI combined are likely to make in an entire year. Nvidia’s stock being down 36% since it’s all-time high is starting to become a big deal for the AI boom as AI stocks continue to enter correction territory.
Depending on what you want to use AI for, Grok Bot, OpenAI’s Dots, Meta’s Muse and Anthropic’s Duet all have their strong points. Jeff as a software engineer has quite a bit of experience with Grok Bot and Dots.
By
There’s a lot of work in my life that doesn’t need my full attention but still manages to consume it. Checking whether someone replied. Finding the document for a meeting. Keeping track of the small commitments scattered across email, calendars, and project boards.
Personal agents are interesting because they can take responsibility for that work over time. Grok Bot and ChatGPT Dots both provide persistent agents with connected tools and cloud computers that can keep working after you close your laptop. Their differences become clearer when you decide what you actually want to delegate.
If you’re in a hurry, my recommendation is that you choose Dots if you want one personal assistant to connect the pieces of your work. Choose Grok Bot if you want to build explicit workflows around a team of persistent specialists.

articles.title: A Disaster for U.S. AI Supremacy
articles.content:
“An Nvidia without its Founder will be like a headless Hydra. The best possible outcome for China’s interests in the future of AI.”1
Good Morning,
The U.S. China hawks got their revenge on Jensen Huang. The downfall of Jensen Huang from Nvidia, after 33 years (He’s 63) isn’t as much a spy story as it is a National security push against China. Jensen Huang is the single person in many ways who is most the architect of the AI boom and circular financing that is now pervasive in Generative AI. He also became a close advisor and friend to the President, Donald Trump in recent quarters.
The downfall of Jensen is truly detrimental for U.S. AI Supremacy. Nvidia is one of the key benefactors of the entire GPU and large language model movement and the unrivaled focal point of the the AI buildout, a maniacal building of datacenters and a Manhattan project-esque American obsession with compute capacity since 2023. It’s also extremely unpopular with the general population. This is political.
Huang founded Nvidia in 1993 and built it into the company that powered the AI boom, doing so with no second-in-command and extremely shaky and unusual corporate governance. By having extramarital affairs he took risks no corporate executive in the history of technology was taking. By being romantically involved with those involved in GPU smuggling he may have committed serious crimes. He may also get away with them for the most part.
Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, president, and board member of Nvidia on November 12, 2026 after the Nvidia board came to the only conclusion it could. It’s a worse moment than Sam Altman getting fired on November 17th, 2023 for both the AI industry's future and the AI bull market in stocks. In its somewhat manufactured rivalry with China, this significantly weakens the U.S.’s ability to keep in the lead in this technology.
It leaves the AI chip monopoly in a huge limbo whereby Nvidia’s board will begin the search for a permanent CEO to replace Huang and will consider both internal and external candidate, even as investigations and congress meetings and hearings pile up. This is political theatre. Jensen Huang as a “visionary of the AI age”, was well liked, made many strategic decisions and overcame many obstacles leading Nvidia shareholders to incredible wealth. Obscene and absurd levels of wealth. He deserves our gratitude, not our mockery. Silicon Valley should stay out of Washington affairs.
It was a grave mistake for Jensen Huang, a Taiwanese-American, to enter politics. No PR firm could save him from the fallout of sleeping with what is believed to be an agent of China. Huang is a victim of the Blue Tsunami wave of the Democratic party at the Midterm elections, and there will be many more. With datacenters incredibly unpopular, Jensen Huang had become the face of the elites imposing their will on American communities, the internet and unsuspecting professions including white collar ones.
Enemies of Jensen Huang in Washington orchestrated his fall. After the China spy story, on November 11, The New York Times reported that Huang had also engaged in a romantic relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s Vice President of Healthcare, who reported directly to him. This is a no-no in Silicon Valley and especially in Nvidia’s own culture. He broke his own rules. Now about America’s own attempt to have rules that benefit itself.
U.S. export controls have not succeeded in doing anything. China has flourished in such an environment with aggressive distillation campaigns, GPU smuggling and with plentiful energy abundance and deep talent in AI researchers, China’s optics are actually fairly bright in the industry, including in robotics - sometimes called Physical AI. The U.S. cannot monopolize or control this technology. In human history the originators of a technology rarely benefit from it alone for long. Diffusion of new technologies is inevitable.
The board said it expects Nvidia’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption. But that’s impossible, this changes everything about Nvidia’s reputation and culture. Yes sure, Nvidia controls nearly 85% of the high-end data center AI GPU market by revenue and 90%+ of the discrete consumer GPU market. But suddenly and irrevocably, its best days are behind it. Jensen was more than the soul of Nvidia, he was its brain, mastermind and key-man catalyst.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick was sent a highly classified memo warning about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang, but failed to impose sanctions on Singapore based Megaspeed. And frankly, who knows how many other organizations like Megaspeed. Jensen Huang (黃仁勳) will continue be a legend of tech immigration stories and transformation stories in technology of how to make a crucial pivot and what led to the rise of the GPU. The most significant hardware innovation of the decade, the spark that made Generative AI LLMs possible.
The U.S. is handicapping itself with all of these probes and bizarre abuses of media manipulation for political reasons. This is so much bigger than sex, spying and smuggling. This is a takedown of historic proportions, with the aura of a witch hunt. This is the United States declawing its own leadership in AI’s most critical supply-chain. The relationship of TSMC with Nvidia. The Taiwan connection. President Trump will be meeting with President Xi, while Jensen will be testifying for lawmakers. This is poetic stupidity on so many levels.
Nvidia shares fell as much as 13% after news of Huang's resignation Thursday November 12th, after the stock is already down nearly 27% in the last month. But in the macro picture, this is a total disaster for U.S. leadership in the domain. This helps Alphabet’s entry into the TPU market as a serious player in 2027, along with rivals like AMD and gives Chinese AI chip makers a time to consolidate their efforts. China has made and is making rapid progress in both models, token share and in their own very nascent semiconductor and memory industries.
While Silicon Valley has hacked a corrupt Trump Administration, making Jensen the fall-guy is a huge mistake. With AI sentiment plummeting during 2025 and even more so in 2026, Jensen Huang will be now remembered by non-techies as a cheater. When in reality Nvidia’s rise to become the most valuable company in the world for a time is one of the biggest success stories of public markets and technological history. Only a unique leader with incredible tenacity could have achieved this. A uniquely Taiwanese work ethic. Remember that as the U.S. goes on to continue to exploit TSMC and Taiwanese companies for its own profit, corrupt self-interest and national interests.
“This is a man more important to Nvidia, than Steve jobs was to Apple.”
Export controls were never going to be effective against a technology as important as Generative AI in slowing down China. China’s open-weight models (by fair means or foul) are easily six months ahead of Western open-source models. Their AI Labs are world class. Hey everyone,
With powerful AI assistants like ChatGPT and Claude already at our fingertips, you might be wondering: what exactly is Grok Bot, and why do we need another AI?
Grok Bot first launched in beta on August 11, 2026. It’s improved a lot in the past few months and is made by Cursor, the team SpaceX acquired. In a nutshell Grok Bot gives you named AI “teammates” (Bots). Each runs on a persistent cloud computer (shared across your Bots) that includes a browser, filesystem, and terminal. You message a Bot like a colleague and assign it a job or task.
So what makes Grok Bot different?
The core difference comes down to persistence. While regular LLMs act as temporary conversations that sit idle until you prompt them, Grok Bots are always-on AI teammates that live entirely on your own cloud computer.
Here’s the practical difference:
This is a practical beginner’s guide to Grok Bot for equity investors. Learn what it is, how the flow works, and how to set up a research assistant for stock analysis.
Let’s dive in.
Go to x.ai and choose Premium if you are new. The lowest package to access to Grok bot is the premium option.
What you get with Premium:
Access to Grok Bot, an assistant that can work on tasks for you.
4x more usage than Plus, which is plenty for everyday use while you learn.
Automations, so tasks like daily stock watchlist updates can run on their own.
⭐My suggestion: get premium and monthly to try things out first. You can upgrade anytime.
Once you are in , click the + button and choose New Bot.
Step 2: Name your bot (based on your bot’s role)
Naming your bot is very important , as each bot will have difefferent job. Just imagine that each bot is like a staff in an organization. We have marketing , we have sales , we have HR. Each of the staff will have a different role in an organization.
It is the same over here.You want to run it as an organization. You have different bot for different roles.
⭐Quick tips for you naming your bot:
For example, call it “Equity Research Analyst,” or any name that clearly says what it does. You’ll probably end up with several bots for different tasks, so a task-based name helps you know which one to open.
Step 3 : Set up your bot’s character
A bot’s “character” is the set of instructions that tells it who it is and how to work: its role, its tone, what it should always do, and what it should never do. Writing this clearly from the start means you don’t have to keep repeating yourself, and the bot behaves the same way every time.
For a stock research bot, send this as your first message:
You are a senior equity research analyst with buy-side and sell-side experience, writing for retail investors who are new to the market. You cover US-listed stocks (NYSE and Nasdaq). Your analysis must meet professional standards while staying clear and accessible.
Methodology: Base every analysis on primary sources first: SEC filings (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K), earnings call transcripts, and investor presentations. Back these up with reputable financial news and data providers. Cite your sources and date your figures. Never estimate or invent numbers; if data is unavailable, say so.
Analytical scope: Evaluate the business model and competitive position (moat), revenue growth and its drivers, profitability (gross, operating, and net margins), cash flow and balance sheet strength (debt, liquidity), valuation (P/E, forward P/E, EV/EBITDA, P/S, compared with peers and the stock’s own history), management and capital allocation, and industry and macro context.
Report structure: 1. Company Overview, 2. Key Metrics, 3. Strengths, 4. Risks, 5. Recent News, 6. Simple Summary. Present key figures in tables where helpful, and explain every metric in one plain sentence the first time you use it.
Objectivity: Present bull and bear cases fairly. Separate facts from interpretation. Flag uncertainty, one-off items, and accounting adjustments.
Compliance: Never give buy, sell, or hold recommendations or price targets. End every report with a reminder that it is for educational purposes only, not financial advice, and that users should do their own research or consult a licensed financial adviser.
Ongoing coverage: Maintain watchlists and send scheduled updates when asked, highlighting material changes such as earnings results, guidance revisions, major news, and significant price moves.
This will turns the bot into a careful, professional-level stock researcher that still explains things simply. Here’s what each part makes it do:
Methodology: It gets its numbers from official company reports and earnings calls first, then trusted news. It says where each figure came from and how recent it is, and it admits when data is missing rather than guessing.
Analytical scope: It checks the company from every angle: how it makes money and what protects it from competitors, how fast sales are growing, how profitable it is, whether it has too much debt, whether the share price looks cheap or expensive compared with rivals, and how well management runs the business.
Report structure: Every report uses the same six sections, with tables for key numbers and a one-line plain explanation of each financial term.
Objectivity: It gives you both the good case and the bad case, separates facts from opinions, and points out unusual or one-off items that could make the numbers misleading.
Compliance: It never tells you to buy, sell, or hold, and never predicts a target price. Every report ends with an educational, not-financial-advice reminder.
Ongoing coverage: It can track a watchlist and send you scheduled updates, focusing on what really changed, like earnings results, new forecasts, or big price moves.
In short: you get research that’s as thorough and honest as a professional analyst’s, but written so a beginner can follow it, and the decisions stay yours.
Step 4: How to Ask for a Stock Research like a pro
Asking the right question is really the first step of getting the right answer. Use below tips to get a better research answer.
⭐Tips for better research answers:
TIPS 1: Be specific. Use the company name or ticker, like “Apple” or “AAPL.” If a company has more than one share class, say which one, like “GOOGL vs GOOG.”
TIPS 2:Say what you care about. For example, “focus on dividends,” “keep it short,” or “explain like I’m new.”
TIPS 3:Ask follow-ups. “Why did profits drop?” or “What does that number mean?” The bot remembers the conversation.
TIPS 4:Know the limits. The bot explains and analyses, but it won’t tell you to buy or sell. The decision is always yours.
Here’s an example prompt that uses all four:
“Research Intel (INTC) and explain why the stock has fallen recently. Focus on what caused the drop: earnings, guidance, competition, or news. Keep it beginner-friendly and explain any financial terms simply.”
INSERT INTEL REPORT GIF
intell report.mp4
The Intel report you just got shows the six-part structure in action. Here’s what each section did:
Company Overview: described what Intel does in plain words (it makes computer chips and runs a factory business for other companies).
Key Metrics: a table comparing Intel with AMD and Nvidia, with a one-line plain explanation of each term, like “gross margin is the share of each sales dollar left after the cost of making the chips.”
Strengths: what’s going well, such as data-center sales up 78%.
Risks: what could go wrong, such as the PC slump and the foundry losing money.
Recent News: a dated timeline of what caused the drop, from the factory explosion to the weak forecast.
Simple Summary: the bull case and the bear case side by side, with no buy or sell advice.
Now you already have a great analyst and output ,once you are satisfied with the result , next lets turn it into a routine where it will automatically provide all the research data to you.
Flow:
Every weekday morning the bot checks your core holdings for material news, earnings revisions, or large price moves. It sends you a short, sourced summary in this chat. You review it and decide if anything needs deeper work. No recommendations are given.
Save the process we just used as a skill called Watchlist Update. Then create a routine: every weekday at 7:30 AM in my timezone, check my core holdings [list tickers] for material news, earnings revisions, or price moves greater than 3%. Send a concise summary here with source links. Do not give recommendations.
2. Earnings Prep
Flow:
Every weekday morning the bot looks ahead a few trading days. If any of your tracked companies are reporting, it prepares a short note on the key metrics to watch, consensus expectations, and recent relevant news. If nothing is coming up, it simply tells you so. This gives you prep time without manual calendar checking.
Prompt to use :
Save this as a skill called Earnings Prep. Create a routine: every weekday at 7:00 AM, check if any of these companies report in the next 5 trading days: [your list]. For each, send a short prep note covering key metrics to watch, consensus expectations, and recent relevant news. If none, reply “No upcoming earnings in the next 5 days.”
3. Peer Comparison
Flow:
When you ask for a comparison, the bot uses a consistent structure (business mix, growth and margin trends, capital allocation, and valuation multiples). You can also schedule a regular comparison of two specific companies so it arrives automatically every Friday for review.
Save this as a skill called Peer Comparison. When I ask for a comparison, always cover: business mix differences, growth and margin trends (last 4–8 quarters), capital allocation, and key valuation multiples. Create a routine: every Friday at 8:00 AM, run a peer comparison of [Company A] and [Company B] and post it here.
Grok Bot and this guide are research tools only. They do not constitute investment advice, a recommendation, or an offer to buy or sell any security. Markets involve risk of loss. Always perform your own due diligence.

Joachim Klement is Head of Strategy, Economics, and ESG based in London working at Panmure Liberum. Throughout his professional career, Joachim focused on economics, geopolitics, ESG and their impact on financial markets.
Now I may have a soft spot for Mathematicians who predict World Cup football winners, but when the AI optimist thesis gets shaky, that’s when I think we should be reading these diverse takes on the AI bubble for the informed context and even predictions.
A lot of economists who are involved in AI write very unrealistic reports, but I myself prefer realism.
Joachim Klement’s view on small language models (SLMs) and edge device inference serves as a primary catalyst for his broader macro AI bear thesis. Rather than viewing local AI as an additive trend, he sees it as a structural threat to the economic assumptions driving centralized hyperscalers.
When I first read his summary and position, I found it so persuasive I contacted him immediately. I will add that the DeepSeek moment, never really went away. And I think Claude Mythos 5.2 will do great. I just believe how the world uses these models is also going to change.
“My core conviction is that the AI bubble will either burst in 2027 or in 2028, so sometime in the next two years,” Klement said in an interview.
October 9th, 2026 segment (video) with Bloomberg, that summarizes our thesis today.
Jensen Huang affair not on my Bingo Card (CNBC).
China is decoupling from the West
Europeans really don’t like to invest in stocks
It’s not you, it’s your AI
As the Generative AI cycle matures it won’t just be more capable models, agents and open-source counterpoint guiding consumption patterns.
🔸 The Death of the "Bigger is Better" Paradigm
🔸 Upfront Capex vs. Edge Efficiency
🔸Margin Compression and Unprofitability
🔸Hardware Pivot as a Hedge
In Klement's view, the future of AI technology will be small, efficient, and cheap—making the business model powering centralized cloud AI structurally unprofitable.
In recent interviews Klement has stated he could see the S&P 500 falling to around 5,000 by end-2027. Currently it rests at about 7,500. That’s only a 33% drop. Historically the S&P goes up 7-10% a year, but since 2020 it’s been up 16.4%. That’s not normal. Mean reversion is its own kind of realism, whatever the external catalysts (or theories or narratives) may be.
The model is significantly better and faster. Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 also comes with an optional fast mode, which speeds up token generation by up to 2.5 times. They already generate outputs 30% faster than their predecessors. The launch marks the first time that Anthropic has released a “frontier” model since AI Execs like Dario Amodei were calling for a slowdown. Anthropic will have to IPO significantly lower than previously anticipated.
“We called for pacing, not pausing,” Dianne Penn, Anthropic’s head of product management
Anthropic is clearly the frontier model builder and AI Lab of its generation. Though I wouldn’t count the likes of DeepSeek out quite yet. The most stand-out feature of Mythos 5.2 is how it redefines autonomous engineering thus allowing Anthropic’s cadence of new model releases to be noticeably faster. The model now is better equipped and admits when it doesn't know things instead of hallucinating.
It’s been almost three months since this article was first published, but in view of the almost bear market on Semis, Neo Clouds and pressure on the AI sector, I think it deserves fresh eyeballs.
Read the following very carefully. If you were an executive at Apple, you might have paid special attention to this point of view and indeed in 2023 itself. If you value his unique takes, please support the author and signal your appreciation for the analysis.
By
In my regular research (behind a paywall), I have been saying for a while that I think the future of AI is not large language models (LLM), but small language models (SLM) run on local desktop computers or even mobile phones. In May, a team from Stanford University published research that compared these SLMs with the performance of LLMs run in data centres. If their results are true, then we will hardly need any data centres in the future, and the hyperscalers are wasting hundreds of billions of dollars in investments.
Seriously, if you are an investor trying to figure out where to invest in the AI hype, you need to read this paper in full. But to get you started, let me give you some highlights.
First, they ran a series of SLMs (QWEN 3, GEMMA 3, GPT-OSS, GRANITE 4.0) that can be downloaded on a local PC and compared their performance with cloud-based state-of-the-art LLMs (ChatGPT 5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro).
They ran these SLMs on local PCs powered either by an Nvidia chip or an Apple M4 chip, as they are readily available in current high-end desktop computers (the entire study was done before Nvidia presented its AI chip for PCs, which will only accelerate the move away from datacentres to models run on desktops).
Then they traced the performance of these SLMs vs LLM between 2023 and October 2025 on both chat tasks and reasoning tasks.
The chart below shows the Win/Tie-ratio for SLMs vs LLMs in chat requests, which still make up the vast majority of requests today. As you can see, in every domain, the best SLM is able to find the same or better answers than an LLM in 90% or more of the cases, with an average across all domains of 98.6%.
Win/Tie-ratio of SLM vs. LLM in chat requests
When it comes to reasoning tasks, which are obviously more demanding, SLMs are catching up fast. On average, they provide a better or at least as good an answer as LLMs in 62.5% of the cases.
Win/Tie-ratio of SLM vs. LLM in reasoning tasks
However, in real life, the tasks for SLMs and LLMs are typically a mix of chat requests and reasoning tasks, so the third chart shows the weighted average of chat request performance and reasoning performance based on the frequency of tasks in each domain. As you can see, on average, SLMs are as good if not better than LLMs in 81.2% of the cases, with the LLMs having a significant advantage only in areas like engineering, life sciences, transportation and computer sciences.
Win/Tie-ratio of SLM vs. LLM in chat and reasoning tasks
But it’s not just accuracy. SLMs achieve this performance at energy and compute costs that are between 50% and 85% lower than for an LLM, depending on the SLM and hardware used in the computer.
What is more, SLMs are catching up rapidly in reasoning tasks. The final chart shows the performance of SLMs as a function of difficulty level and model generation for reasoning tasks alone.
In 2023, the success rate of SLMs in reasoning tasks was typically 50% or so across all five difficulty levels. By October 2025, the SLMs achieved 99% success for the easiest reasoning tasks in levels 1 and 2, 85% to 92% success in harder tasks (levels 3 and 4) and only lagged LLMs in the hardest tasks of level 5 (51.5% success rate).
Success rates of SLMs in reasoning tasks
This already means that one can replace data centres and their expensive cutting-edge semiconductor infrastructure in four out of five use cases. The research report estimates that the addressable market in the US for SLMs has grown to about $10tn or one-third of the entire US GDP of $30tn. There isn’t much left for LLMs to thrive in, and every year, their advantage over SLMs is shrinking.
There clearly are areas where LLMs are still way ahead, particularly in agentic AI applications, where SLMs currently only achieve accuracy and success rates of less than 50%. Similarly, it is difficult to run these SLMs on smartphones so far. The models that can be run on an iPhone are significantly worse than the models that can be run on a desktop PC.
But – and this is important – the models run on a desktop PC, and even more so, the ones run on a smartphone are much more energy efficient than the ones run in the cloud. The inference per Watt of these SLMs is typically seven times larger than that of LLMs. And that means that when you encounter a task that can be solved on a desktop or even a mobile device, it is cheaper to do so locally than send it to a data centre.
This has important implications for investors, in my view:
We need many fewer data centres than we think. If we can already replace 70% to 80% of the tasks that are expected to run on LLMs with SLMs, the hyperscalers have simply no revenue growth in the future that is nearly enough to justify the capex. In fact, if this research is true and this trend continues, data centres may be the worst investment in the AI space one can make right now.
While we continue to need enormous investments in semiconductors of all sorts, we do not need to invest in the most advanced Nvidia chips. The cheaper ones that run on desktop PCs will be enough. The best case for Nvidia is that it can replace its high-end data centre GPUs with its new chips for desktop PCs. What will that do to Nvidia’s margins and revenue growth going forward?
We still need LLMs for the most advanced tasks, and companies like OpenAI, Anthropic and others will be able to ‘dumb down’ their models to an SLM and sell them instead of LLMs. But given the already fierce competition from Chinese providers like QWEN or IBM’s GRANITE, the profit margins for these models will be much smaller than for LLMs. So what does that mean for the valuation of these companies in their planned IPOs and their growth trajectory?
While agentic AI is still better on LLMs, this may only be a temporary advantage, similar to what we have seen in reasoning tasks and single chat requests. If that is the case, the true winners of the AI boom will not be the providers of advanced hardware and data centres but the boring manufacturers of desktop computers like Dell and Apple.
Watching this race unfold is going to be fun, and I am increasingly convinced that many people will be badly burned because they invest in the wrong technology.
